question.prompt: How many of the following are equal to \(x^x+x^x\) for all \(x\gt0?\) \[ \begin{aligned} \mathrm{I:}\quad&2x^x\\ \mathrm{II:}\quad&x^{2x}\\ \mathrm{III:}\quad&(2x)^x\\ \mathrm{IV:}\quad&(2x)^{2x} \end{aligned} \]

solutions.explanation:
The phrase “for all \(x>0\)” requires an equality to hold at every positive input. One positive input where it fails is enough to rule it out.

Adding two copies of the same quantity gives
\[
x^x+x^x=2x^x
\]
for every \(x>0\), so I always works.

To test the other three statements, take \(x=2\). The original expression is \(2^2+2^2=8\), while
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{II}:&\quad 2^4=16,\\
\mathrm{III}:&\quad 4^2=16,\\
\mathrm{IV}:&\quad 4^4=256.
\end{aligned}
\]
Each differs from \(8\), so none of II, III, or IV holds for all positive \(x\). Exactly \(\boxed{1}\) statement qualifies, choice \(\text{B}\).
solutions.title: Prove I and test the other statements
